title: Treatment Decision Information
rationale: Retain the contrast between a recorded choice and a response process. The NIST glossary entry is security-specific and attributed there to SP 800-39; it does not establish that a Riskium decision was authorized, executed or successful.
context_interpretation: R-19 relates the decision to the continuing RiskCase; R-20 selects a strategy. R-63 and RK2-014/RK2-015 may connect plans, evaluation and remaining-risk assessment. Those documentary links do not alone establish treatment execution or effectiveness.

title: Treatment Strategy Term
rationale: Retain SKOS vocabulary context for a scheme-qualified treatment approach. A selected strategy resource is distinct from a decision or action; no universal security-only list or formal SKOS equivalence is adopted.
context_interpretation: R-20 selects this term in decision information. ClassificationTerm/VocabularyConcept ancestry preserves managed resource identity, while common labels and retained sibling groups do not create equivalence, exclusivity or realized response.

title: Plan Specification
rationale: Retain PROV Plan as related intended-action content. Riskium records its own resources, responsibility, timing, purpose and versions without adopting a full PROV representation or treating the plan as its execution.
context_interpretation: R-21 concerns one or more analytical risk cases; R-62 gives the plan role. R-64 relates an actual TreatmentActivity separately, and R-63 can connect decisions. A plan can be recorded before any execution is established; issued-content changes follow new-version lineage.

title: Plan Role Term
rationale: Retain vocabulary-resource context for primary-response, contingency or other plan functions. SKOS does not define those local functions, and a PlanRoleTerm is not an OntoUML agent role or performance of a response.
context_interpretation: R-62 assigns the chosen function to a plan specification. Scheme-qualified identity is inherited through ClassificationTerm/VocabularyConcept; the retained incomplete/non-disjoint groups are carried policy, not a new semantic-partition approval.

title: Risk Criteria
rationale: Retain the explicit licensed-source deferral. The ISO catalogue reconfirms edition identity and generic vocabulary purpose only; no exact risk-criteria wording, clause locator or standards crosswalk is adopted from metadata.
context_interpretation: RX-017 qualifies the criteria specification by context. RX-018/RX-019 permit appetite/tolerance statements without making them universally mandatory or identical. The local C-25 version-target obligation remains separate from any uninspected normative definition.

title: Risk Appetite Statement
rationale: Retain the explicit normative deferral to #78. The managed appetite statement and its source qualification remain Riskium-authored; no catalogue abstract is promoted into an ISO/Risk IT/COBIT term definition or proof of authority.
context_interpretation: RK2-023 requires context under this managed profile, and RX-018 can connect criteria to the statement. Its objective, authority and framework qualifications preserve provenance; a statement is not universal permission for every case or evidence that an organization acted on it.

title: Risk Tolerance Statement
rationale: Retain the explicit normative deferral and source-specific tolerance meanings. Permissible-deviation and remaining-risk readings are not silently equated or attributed to an unseen ISO clause; exact edition-qualified interpretation remains #78.
context_interpretation: RK2-024 requires context under the managed profile and RX-019 optionally connects criteria. C-10 preserves framework/version/original meaning; common tolerance labels do not justify pooling values or applying a threshold to an unrelated context.

title: Objective Reference
rationale: Retain the distinction between an informational reference and the objective it identifies. Generic PROV Entity has broad provenance scope and does not alone determine referent identity or objective achievement.
context_interpretation: RX-003 connects analytical RiskCase to objective references; RK2-011 allows context-specific references. Revised RiskCase meaning was reviewed. The reference can identify source-context objectives without importing an entire organization ontology or asserting that the objective has been achieved.

title: Control Reference
rationale: Retain the contrast between a managed control identifier/description and a safeguard. NIST security-controls text retains its FIPS 199/CNSSI 4009 attribution; neither it nor PROV Entity proves a resolved bearer, implementation or effectiveness.
context_interpretation: RX-020 keeps resolution to the heterogeneous control boundary optional. RK2-016/RK2-022 retain register and assessment-baseline references. C-14 excludes a uniform formal-core RiskControl class, so unresolved references remain information rather than fabricated realized controls.
